items.item_text: 01. Tell us about your understanding of how systems of oppression impact student achievement. In what ways have you or will you challenge these systems to improve equitable outcomes in community colleges in your discipline(s)? (Max 300 words)

02. Tell us about why diversity is important to you. How does this or will this "why" manifest in your interactions with students whether in the classroom, counseling spaces, librarian spaces or elsewhere as faculty?

03. Where did you hear about this position? Options: Our Career Page | Asian Week | California Community College Chancellor's Office website | Career Builder | Chronicle of Higher Education website | Chronicle of Higher Education newspaper | Community College Jobs Website | Word of Mouth | Community College Times | Craigslist | Diverse Issues in Higher Education | El Mundo | Walk-In (PCCD Office of Human Resources) | Hispanic Outlook in Higher Education | Indeed.com | Oakland Post Walk-In (PCCD Office of Human Resources) | Job Fair, Conference, or Workshop | Local Newspaper (Oakland Tribune, SF Chronicle, ect) | Women in Higher Education | 24-Hour Job Line | Other
Gain hands-on experience teaching counseling or working with students in an ethnically diverse community college
Share knowledge and skills in a professional setting under the supervision of an experienced faculty member
Earn remuneration (if a class or position is available)
Meet and build with other professionals through our cohort model
Work closely and meet regularly with a Faculty Mentor
Current registration and in good standing at a college during the term(s) of the internship;

Demonstrated cultural competency, sensitivity to, and understanding of, the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, and ethnic backgrounds of community college staff, faculty, and students.
